new_finding_not_blocking: Pre-existing, separate root cause, recommend a new BACKLOG row (P1, Snitch only): RA spills and split copies inside an accepted frep body under FP register pressure at -O1..-O3 cause wrong code. Reproducer logs/20-F023-review2/press30.ll: 30 plain accumulators and 4 loop-invariant multipliers, llc -O2. The pass accepts it (every PHI is a plain accumulator) and emits frep.o N=30, but after RA the body holds 30 fmul.d plus fld reloads (fld fs0, 32(sp)) and a chain of fmv.d. These are sequenced but not counted, so the repeated window ends early and the rest runs once. toolchains/port-20fix2 gives the same output (logs/20-F023-review2/press30.port-20fix2.s), so this is not caused by F023. 28 accumulators + 4 invariants (32 live FP values) is still clean; 30 is not. The note lists this as a residual risk that was 'not observed'. It is now observed. The note's wording is acceptable because the risk is disclosed, and this review corrects it to observed. A pre-RA pass cannot see the spills. Possible fixes (conductor's choice): (a) a pre-RA FP pressure bound (live FP PHIs + invariant FP live-ins + body temporaries <= available FPRs minus the SSR-reserved ones), or (b) a post-RA recount of N over the body (spill fld/fsd and fmv.d are sequenced, so a post-RA recount would be exact), with an error if a non-sequenced instruction lands inside.

reasons: llvm/lib/Target/RISCV/Snitch/SNITCHFrepLoops.cpp:786-796 (PHI handling in containsInvalidInstruction) and :799-822 (FP COPY accepted and not counted): the under-count the worker lists as a residual risk is real wrong code, and it happens in a loop the pass still accepts. The GVSoC model (gvsoc/gvsoc/models/cpu/iss/isa_gen/isa_riscv_gen.py:767) tags fsgnj.d (fmv.d) as 'fp_op' and not 'nseq', so sequencer.cpp:37-52 puts it in the sequence buffer and it counts towards N. Reproducer logs/20-F023-review/swap.ll (pure-FP body, loop-carried swap a,b = b,a+b; and a 3-value rotate) at llc -O2 gives 'frep.o a0, 1' over 'fadd.d fa1, fa0, fa1; fmv.d fa0, fa4' (swap), and over 'fmul.d; fmv.d; fmv.d' (rot). N=1, so the hardware repeats only the fadd/fmul 64 times and the fmv.d copies run once: the result is wrong (b+64a instead of the recurrence). Output is identical on build/int-20, so the defect is pre-existing, but it is exactly what this task was meant to close ('only convert when the hardware will really repeat the whole body'; the conductor asked for the COPY under-count to be fixed here or declined). These copies are created after the pass by PHI elimination/register allocation from loop-carried FP PHIs that cannot be coalesced. At pass time they are PHIs (ignored at :788), not COPYs, so declining FP COPYs alone would not fix it. The pass must decline (it cannot count pre-RA what RA will add) at least: (a) any FP COPY in the body (never observed at pass time on any input: a -debug-only=snitch-freploops scan of the four fork FREP tests, all F014 rev3/review inputs, ivuse.ll and swap.ll at -O0..-O3 found no 'ignoring FP COPY', so declining costs nothing measurable), and (b) any loop-carried FP header PHI whose value stays live after its back-edge value is defined: the back-edge value is another header PHI (swap/rotate), or the PHI result is used after the back-edge def or outside the loop. Otherwise the copy cannot be coalesced. Plain accumulators (the @inv, freploop, freploop-nested and F014 shapes) must still convert, and the fork FREP tests must stay byte-identical.
